notes.title: The day we've been waiting for is here! (And also the first Animas Playtest)
notes.notes: [p]Hey everyone![/p][p]The day the global gaming community has been eagerly awaiting is finally here. That's right, you guessed it: today marks the launch of the first-ever [b]public Playtest[/b] for [i]Animas[/i]! You can request access right now on our Steam page, and if all goes well, you'll get to explore the Blanco family home for the very first time.[/p][p]After months of intense work on this project, we're dying to share it and start hearing your first impressions. We know there's still a LONG way to go, but we feel that developing without player feedback is like working in the dark, and your eyes will help us find the way.[/p][p][/p][h3]What will you find in this Playtest?[/h3][p][/p][p]This test is a very early version of what will become [b]"Animas: Prologue,"[/b] a free, standalone chapter that we'll release later as a demo. This prologue tells a self-contained story that won't be in the final game, but it serves as the perfect introduction to the mystery of the Blanco family and the world of [i]Animas[/i].[/p][p][/p][h3]An Important Warning on Spoilers[/h3][p][/p][p]We want to be completely transparent: this playtest includes almost the entire story of the prologue. If you're the type who avoids spoilers at all costs to enjoy the full, polished experience, [b]you might want to wait for the official release of the Prologue.[/b][/p][p]For the brave souls who decide to jump in now, your feedback is golden. At the end of the test, you'll find a link to a feedback form with several questions that would be a huge help to us. You can also leave your comments, report bugs, or just hang out with us on our [url="https://discord.gg/t7HUA9DeUH"]Discord[/url].[/p][p][/p][h3]Current Status and Known Issues[/h3][p][/p][p]As we mentioned, this is an early build. To save you time reporting things already on our radar, here’s a list of what we know is incomplete or needs fixing:[/p][list][*][p][b]3D Models and Textures:[/b] Several objects are temporary ([i]placeholders[/i]) and don't have their final textures yet (you'll see them as solid white or gray).[/p][/*][*][p][b]Sound:[/b] Many sound effects are missing (especially for doors), and the music has not been implemented yet.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Animations:[/b] Some animations are still pending; you'll notice this most in the dinner scene.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Dialogue Volume:[/b] We are still adjusting the levels of some voice lines.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Save System:[/b] It's not functional yet. If you exit to the main menu, you will have to start the game over from the beginning.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Options Menu:[/b] It has not been implemented yet, so you cannot change graphics or other settings.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p]Thanks again for joining us on this journey. Your support means the world to a small studio like ours.[/p][p]In the meantime, we'll be playing Sil... ahem... [b]working very hard on [i]Animas[/i][/b]. o.o[/p][p][/p][p]Best, [/p][p][/p][p]Wilmar & Wilderman[/p][p]Apamate Studio[/p]

notes.title: September Update: Giving Animas a Voice & A Playtest is Coming!
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p]This past month has been incredibly productive, and we're getting closer and closer to the release of the [i]Animas[/i] demo. While we don't want to announce a specific date just yet—we want to make sure every detail is polished to perfection—we can tell you that it's just around the corner. In fact, September has probably been one of the months with the most significant progress since we started development.[/p][p]The most important and exciting milestone of the month was, without a doubt, [b]recording the voice lines[/b]. It was a deeply satisfying process to see the story we wrote almost a year ago finally come to life through talented actors. We want the experience to be authentic in every sense, and that includes real human voices that convey every nuance of the horror we're building.[/p][p]Here’s a short behind-the-scenes look at the recording process:[/p][previewyoutube="QNOGZrOUGLs;full"][/previewyoutube][p]With the voices recorded and integrated, we've been able to assemble the complete narrative skeleton of the demo. This means it's now playable from start to finish—a huge step forward for us.[/p][p]Now, our work is focused on breathing life and soul into that skeleton. Over the last few weeks, we've been diving deep into:[/p][list][*][p][b]Populating the environments:[/b] Adding the final 3D models and detailed textures so that every corner of the house tells its own story.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Crafting the atmosphere:[/b] Playing with lighting and shadows to build the oppressive tension we're aiming for.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Polishing the immersion:[/b] Implementing key animations and, of course, fine-tuning the scares to make them truly effective.[/p][/*][/list][p]You can see some of that work here:[/p][p][/p][carousel][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/0aac9a5b8fca9f92dfc5ecbac21de7d180272b3c.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/2dc7a8baf1f9e15e091fde15361371ccfa2ae747.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/8f30684466d1c1051b9f2afb7bac4f811282bccf.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/417778d54547c0c8dddeedd3309bf542e3e31b00.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/88fbbfb900d371871cf7f0a7f6ba9afdda682ea9.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/8c84b253f22d469cd4f1476b8a428b34c5584f75.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/49f09be5073af6224042f10525dfb66df167431d.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/aedc9b4bf7e0aa5d8861b55eed9894c705e9d7f3.png"][/img][/carousel][p]And now, for one last very important piece of news. Very soon, we will be granting access to test [i]Animas[/i] for the first time through a [b]public playtest[/b]. We are eager to receive your first impressions and feedback, which will be incredibly valuable to us. This will be a unique opportunity for you to get a "behind-the-scenes" look at the game and help us shape the final experience.[/p][p]Stay tuned, because we'll be making the official announcement in the coming days.[/p][p]As always, thank you for joining us on this journey![/p][p]– The Apamate Studio Team[/p]

notes.title: From the Animas workshop: A look at our July progress
notes.notes: [p]Hello everyone![/p][p][/p][p]It's been a month since our last update, and we've been working non-stop on the Blanco family's house, filling every corner with the secrets and atmosphere that will make [i]Animas[/i] a truly unsettling experience. We wanted to share a glimpse of what we've been up to.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Building the atmosphere, detail by detail.[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]One of our main goals this month has been to make steady progress on the game's prologue. We have already locked down the structure and progression for this first experience, and we can estimate that it will have an [b]approximate length of 40 minutes[/b]. Right now, our focus is on the details: transforming the house from a simple set piece into another character in the story. We want those 40 minutes to be packed with content and clues that enrich the narrative, making sure that every object and every shadow has something to say.[/p][p][/p][p]To achieve that authenticity, sometimes you have to obsess over the small details. As many of you know, candles are a fundamental element in Venezuela's religious traditions and rituals. They are a symbol of faith, a bridge to the spiritual, and in [i]Animas[/i], a source of light in the midst of overwhelming darkness. That's why it was unthinkable for us not to dedicate the necessary time to create a good candle system. Our goal was to have a wide variety of them, to make their flickering feel natural, and most importantly, to be able to animate them in a controlled and interesting way during the key moments when they are lit and extinguished.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/9def4a168aaf547a6df646ca9dbaff673e07f5b9.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]But terror doesn't live on candles alone. We have also been deep into 3D modeling, creating a large number of religious statuettes. These figures will be one of the most representative visual elements of the game, anchoring the world of [i]Animas[/i] directly in the complex and fascinating spiritual traditions of Venezuela. Each one has its own story and its own weight in the mystery you are about to uncover.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/eb151ae9f922ec4cca812fe2dc7e334a9004ee78.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/c0b540ac48e2294665b7d3f23c8995a3a3d5be39.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/c65f4dc313444b896e44c9cc8c77fdb427dcf16d.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535654/bf2bc3704abca71d8897bf27c4f6d3603914851d.png"][/img][/carousel][p][/p][h3][b]The voices that will guide us in the darkness[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]A fundamental pillar for immersion in [i]Animas[/i] is the sound, and more specifically, the voices that will bring its characters to life. We are pleased to announce that we are now preparing everything to [b]record the voice-over for the prologue in the coming weeks[/b]. We are incredibly excited to be able to work with professional voice actors who will give the story the depth and character it deserves. We hope to share some pictures and stories from the recording sessions with you soon![/p][p][/p][h3][b]What's next: a final push for the prologue[/b][/h3][h3][/h3][p]With all this progress, the announcement of the prologue's release date is getting closer and closer. And to give it that final push, we have planned a two-week "crunch" period for next month. These will be days where we disconnect from everything else to dedicate ourselves 100% to development. This means that our next update on the game's progress promises to be the juiciest and most significant one we've shared so far.[/p][p][/p][p]We're eager to show you the results of all this hard work. As always, thank you for your support and for joining us on this journey.[/p][p][/p][p]Talk to you soon, [/p][p][b]The Apamate Studio Team[/b][/p]

notes.title: What have we been up to? An Animas Dev Update
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

It's been a while since we shared our announcement trailer, and first of all, we wanted to thank you. The truth is, the reception Animas received took us by surprise, in the best possible way. In these few months, thanks to you, we've surpassed [b]3000 wishlists[/b], a milestone that has filled us with motivation and energy.

While you were showing us your incredible support, we've been completely immersed in the Blanco family home. As we've progressed, we've realized something: the potential of this project is much greater than we had anticipated. Therefore, to do justice to the game you've shown us you want to see, we've made the decision to adjust our launch schedule for the full game.

But the good news is that you won't have to wait that long to set foot in the house. Our immediate plan, where we are focusing all our efforts, is to release [b]Animas: Prologue[/b] this year. It will be a standalone, self-contained experience that will serve as a first dive into the unsettling universe of Animas.

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45535654/56e6d2e7eb1c287b2de2e3e468a452d7085d4a52.png[/img][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45535654/8bb5de3de4720263bdad9f0fefecb31e8c3fc9aa.png[/img][/carousel]

Setting a game in the Venezuelan mountains across different eras means that almost every object you'll see—from the furniture and the food on the table, to the specific religious icons that adorn the walls—is being modeled and textured by hand by us. It's meticulous and time-consuming work, but it's the only way to achieve the cultural authenticity we consider to be the core of this project.

As you can imagine, a larger project and an extended development schedule also mean a greater need for resources. As a self-funded independent studio, to get Animas to the finish line with the quality we all expect, we are actively exploring our options. This includes looking for a publisher who shares our vision, as well as the possibility of a crowdfunding campaign in the future.

For now, the most powerful and direct way you can help us is super simple: [b]add and keep Animas on your Steam Wishlist.[/b] Spreading the word about the game also helps us a lot. Every wishlist is a vote of confidence that boosts us enormously on the platform; it tells Steam and potential partners that there is a real and excited community waiting for this game.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/45535654/0c4dedfde703331f69b0e7461bd5c73f57fcf0ed.gif[/img]

Again, thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your patience, your trust, and for joining us on this journey. We are pouring all our passion into this project and we're dying to have you visit the Blanco family home for the first time in [b]Animas: Prologue[/b].

All the best,

Wilmar & Wilderman
Apamate Studio

notes.title: Animas Now on Steam: A Psychological Horror Game Set in Venezuela
notes.notes:
Greetings, Steam community! Today is a very special day for Apamate Studio, as we can finally present [b]Animas[/b], our new video game. Prepare to immerse yourself in a unique psychological horror experience [b]set in the mysterious mountains of Venezuela.[/b]

For those familiar with our work on [b]Mechanophagia[/b], let us share that [b]Animas[/b] represents a new chapter for our studio. While [b]Mechanophagia[/b] was our first project – born as a learning prototype and developed with great care over a year – with Animas, we wanted to explore different horizons. As a growing studio, we're excited to experiment and gradually define our identity as creators.

With [b]Animas[/b], we set two main goals. First, to channel our prior artistic experience in film and animation into creating a game with a strong narrative and visual component. We leveraged our 3D modeling and animation expertise to build an immersive, unsettling atmosphere. Second, we wanted to deeply connect with our cultural roots. As Venezuelans, we felt motivated to contribute our perspective to the gaming industry – a field where we believe representation of our culture remains scarce.

Stay tuned, as in the coming weeks and months we'll share many more details about Animas. To avoid missing updates, [b]add Animas to your wishlist![/b] This way, you'll receive direct notifications about the demo release and other important news (we have very exciting plans for the demo, so keep an eye out!).

Finally, if you'd like to directly support Animas' development and help bring this project to life, consider checking out Mechanophagia. It's our first game, and while it's very different from Animas and perhaps more modest in scale, we hold it dear. If you enjoy discovering indie studios' early works and want to support our journey, Mechanophagia could be a great way to do so.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2757540/Mechanophagia/

We'll return soon with more [b]Animas[/b] news! Thank you for joining us on this journey!
